SELECTED_INDEX: 4
CONFIDENCE: 0.75
EXPLANATION: The strong band at 1786 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of an acyl chloride-type carbonyl and fits methyl chloroformate much better than ordinary esters (2, 6, 8) or other candidates lacking C=O; no nitrile band near ~2250 cm⁻¹ excludes 10. The very intense bands at 2972 and 2854 cm⁻¹ match aliphatic C–H stretches (GFQ-003). Multiple strong features in the 780–830 cm⁻¹ region (788, 821 cm⁻¹) are consistent with C–Cl stretching vibrations (cf. CCl₄ range in GFQ-046), supporting a –COCl group. The 1458 cm⁻¹ band is consistent with CH₃ deformation (GFQ-003), and bands at 1156 and 1214 cm⁻¹ align with C–O stretching of the chloroformate moiety. Overall, the high ν(C=O) and C–Cl region make 4 the best match.
